summary: Google OAuth is the most demanding setup in this library. Apps using only non-sensitive scopes need no verification, but any sensitive or restricted scope (Gmail, Drive, Calendar data) requires Google's OAuth app verification, and restricted scopes also require an annual third-party security assessment. Google does not publish review timelines; community reports put the full process at weeks and costs in the thousands of dollars.
key_facts: Two tracks: non-sensitive scopes need no verification; sensitive and restricted scopes require Google's OAuth app verification
Restricted scopes (e.g. broad Gmail / Drive access) also require an annual security assessment by a Google-empanelled assessor — cost and duration vary and are not published by Google
Verification is repeated annually for apps with restricted scopes, and some configuration changes trigger re-verification
Your homepage must be on a verified domain, describe your app (not just a login page) and link your privacy policy; the same policy must be linked on the consent screen
Every authorized domain must be verified through Google Search Console
Sensitive/restricted scopes need a demo video showing the full OAuth flow and consent screen (English) with the exact scopes requested
You must justify each scope and why narrower scopes would not work — vague justification can cause rejection
Apps in 'Testing' mode are limited to test users and show an unverified-app warning

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud Project
steps.description: Go to Google Cloud Console → Create Project. Use a dedicated project for your OAuth app (separate from other GCP usage). Enable the specific APIs you need (e.g., Gmail API, Google Drive API, Google Calendar API) under APIs & Services → Library.
warnings: Create separate projects for development and production
Enable only the APIs you actually use — each unused enabled API is a liability during review

steps.title: Configure OAuth Consent Screen
steps.description: In APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen, select 'External' (for users outside your org). Fill in: App name, user support email, app logo (512x512px PNG), app homepage URL, privacy policy URL, terms of service URL, and authorized domains. Add the scopes your app needs.
warnings: Homepage, privacy policy, and ToS must be live public URLs — not localhost or placeholder pages
App logo must be exactly 512x512 pixels PNG
Authorized domains must be domains you own (verified in Google Search Console)

steps.title: Create OAuth 2.0 Credentials
steps.description: Go to APIs & Services → Credentials → Create Credentials → OAuth client ID. Select 'Web application'. Add authorized JavaScript origins (your app domain) and authorized redirect URIs. For Composio, add: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback

steps.title: Test in Development Mode
steps.description: While in 'Testing' publishing status, add test user emails (up to 100) in the OAuth consent screen settings. Only these users can authenticate. Your app works but users see an 'unverified app' warning screen.
warnings: Users outside your test list cannot authenticate at all — plan this carefully for beta testing

steps.title: Determine Your Scope Tier
steps.description: Review your requested scopes against Google's scope classification. Non-sensitive scopes (email, profile, openid) → fast approval (days). Sensitive scopes (contacts.readonly, calendar.readonly) → manual review (days to 1 week). Restricted scopes (gmail.modify, drive) → CASA security assessment (4–6 weeks, $4K+ cost).
warnings: Requesting ANY restricted scope puts your entire app into the CASA audit track
Consider if read-only scopes satisfy your use case to avoid the restricted track

steps.title: Prepare Verification Assets
steps.description: Record a short video (2–5 min, unlisted YouTube) showing: user visiting your app → clicking 'Sign in with Google' → seeing OAuth consent screen → granting permissions → landing back in your app. This is mandatory for verification submission.
warnings: Video must show the complete OAuth flow clearly — blurry or cut-off videos cause rejection

steps.title: Submit for Verification
steps.description: Change publishing status from 'Testing' to 'In production' and click 'Submit for verification'. Complete Google's verification questionnaire: describe your app, explain why each scope is needed, provide your demo video URL, and submit.
warnings: If requesting restricted scopes, you'll be directed to complete a annual security assessment before Google reviews your app

steps.title: Complete Security Assessment (if restricted scopes)
steps.description: If your app needs restricted scopes, hire an approved CASA assessor from Google's partner list. They conduct a security assessment of your application. Cost and duration vary by assessor and app (commonly reported in the thousands of dollars; Google does not publish them). Timeline: 4–6 weeks.
warnings: This is a mandatory step — there is no workaround for restricted scopes targeting external users
Budget both time and money for this step well in advance

requirements.account_type: Free Google account sufficient for setup; CASA audit cost is the real barrier

blockers.title: Security Assessment (Restricted Scopes)
blockers.description: Apps requesting restricted scopes (Gmail write, full Drive access) must complete a annual security assessment before Google will approve verification. This is a separate, paid third-party assessment whose cost and duration Google does not publish.
blockers.workaround: Use read-only scopes where possible. Use Composio managed auth to avoid this entirely during prototyping. For production, either budget for the audit or scope down your permission requirements.

blockers.title: 100-User Limit in Testing Mode
blockers.description: Until verified, your app can only authenticate up to 100 pre-approved test users. Attempting to authenticate other users results in an error.
blockers.workaround: Add all team members and beta users to the test users list. Use Composio managed auth for early customer testing.

blockers.title: Domain Ownership Verification
blockers.description: Authorized domains in your consent screen must be domains you control, verified through Google Search Console. Localhost and unverified domains are rejected.
blockers.workaround: Verify your production domain in Google Search Console before starting the consent screen setup.
